title: Mail Merges, Modernized
text:
This package provides a modern alternative to standard Word mail merge, using Jinja2-like templating syntax to enable advanced features and streamline document generation workflows.
This started with the reality of nationwide regulatory work: every province has its own rules, which meant its own templates — and within each, a matrix of entitlement types (locked-in, non-locked-in, cash only, partial payments, immediate vs. deferred pensions) that multiplied the template count fast.
Imagine this. Dozens of templates across provinces and entitlement types. Templates get tweaked constantly, and actuarial numbers aren’t always right the first time, which means reopening each document, clicking through Word’s merge wizard, exporting to PDF, and renaming every file by hand, over and over, under a tight deadline.
That’s hours of tedious, repetitive work — and it only gets worse as templates multiply.
So I built a tool that turns all of that into a single command. Update a template or fix a number, and the entire batch re-merges automatically — no reopening files, no manual exporting, no renaming. What used to take hours now takes minutes, and it scales just as easily to five templates as it does to fifty.

section: Why Use This Instead of Standard Mail Merge?
text:
Why Use This Instead of Standard Mail Merge?

Key Advantages

Powerful templating syntax: Jinja2-like tags enable conditional logic, loops, and dynamic content
Rich formatting support: Maintain text formatting, insert images, and create dynamic tables
Automatic field detection: Quickly extract all required fields from templates without manual inspection
Scalability: Efficiently manage large numbers of templates across multiple groups
Type safety: Better validation and error handling compared to traditional merge fields

title: Mail Merges, Modernized
text:
Template Workflow

Step 1: Adding Tags to Your DOCX Templates
Unlike standard Word merge fields (which use « MERGEFIELD » syntax), this package uses Jinja2-style tags that are more readable and powerful.

Basic Tag Syntax
{{ field_name }}
Simply type these tags directly into your Word document where you want dynamic content to appear.


Example Template
Dear {{ recipient_name }},

Thank you for your purchase of {{ product_name }} on {{ purchase_date }}.

Your order total: {{ order_total }}

Best regards,
{{ sender_name }}


Conditional Content
Use if-statements to show or hide content based on your data:
{% if premium_customer %}
As a valued premium customer, you receive free shipping on all orders!
{% endif %}


Dynamic Tables
Generate table rows dynamically from list data:
| Item | Quantity | Price |
|------|----------|-------|
{%tr for item in items %}
| {{ item.name }} | {{ item.quantity }} | {{ item.price }} |
{%tr endfor %}


Rich Text Variables
Variables can contain inline formatting — bold, italic, underline, color, font size — so styled content merges cleanly into your document without splitting it across multiple fields.
{{r richtext}}


Dynamic Images
Swap in different images at merge time based on your data — useful for logos, signatures, charts, or any image that varies per recipient.
{{ logo }}



Step 2: Field Extraction
Automatically scan a template, or folder of templates (searches recursively in sub-folders), and list every field it requires — no need to track them manually.
This is especially handy when working with a large number of templates, each with their own unique set of fields.

tags = getFieldTags(extractFromDocx(tpl_dir))
sorted(tags)

['{% endif %}',
 '{% if amt_cash %}',
 '{% if pct_rome %}',
 '{{ amt_cash }}',
 '{{ amt_li_ls }}',
 '{{ amt_partial_ls }}',
 '{{ dt_doe }}',
 '{{ dt_doh }}',
 '{{ dt_dot }}',
 '{{ dt_mdob }}',
 '{{ dt_nrd }}',
 '{{ dt_partial_ls }}',
 '{{ dt_send }}',
 '{{ img_logo }}',
 '{{ pct_rome }}',
 '{{ str_footer }}',
 '{{ str_greet }}',
 '{{ str_id }}',
 '{{ str_ls_msg }}',
 '{{ str_mailing_details }}',
 '{{ str_mbr_name }}',
 '{{ str_sex }}']




Step 3: Running the Merge
Once your templates are tagged and your data is prepared, running the merge is a single command:
merge("./path/to/config.yml")

Pass _test=n to run only the first n records — useful for quickly checking formatting before a full run.
Pass a list into _test_ids to check specific IDs (special cases, etc.)


Config file
The merge function takes a YAML config file as its primary parameter. This keeps your merge setup readable and easy to edit without touching code, serves as a clear record of where your data lives, how templates map to recipient groups, and can be version-controlled.
Here is a simple example:
data: C:/path/to/data.parquet
id_col: id
group_col: _group
groups:
- example:
  - C:/path/to/template.docx
image_cols:
- img_logo
There is also a helper function (helpers.initCfg) to help generate this config file automatically.

title: RichText

Example:
Note that RichText ignores styling and uses the default style in the Word template unless explicitly specified.
Use the patched RT class in this module and initialize with a RTFormatOpts instance to set up default styling options.

title: RichText
text:
Bold certain text
def boldText(text: str) -> RichText:
    """For proof of age / proof of death fields

    Parameters
    ----------
    text : str
        str

    Returns
    -------
    RichText
        RichText
    """
    _opts = RTFormatOpts(size=20)
    rt = RT(_opts)
    if text.strip().lower() == "yes":
        rt.addText(text)
        return rt
    else:
        rt.addText(text, bold=True)
        return rt


cols = ["str_mpoa", "str_spoa", "str_mpod"]
for c in cols:
    df[c] = df[c].apply(lambda x: boldText(x)).astype(str)

title: RichText
text:
Multi-line w/ various formatting options

def createSampleRT(tr: pd.Series) -> RichText:
    """-> RichText

    Parameters
    ----------
    tr : pd.Series
        pd.Series

    Returns
    -------
    RichText
        RichText
    """
    name = tr["name"]
    _id = tr["id"]
    group = tr["group"]

    _opts = RTFormatOpts(size=30)
    rt = RT(_opts)

    rt.addText("Member ID: ")
    rt.addText(_id, bold=True)
    rt.addText("\n")
    rt.addText("Name: ")
    rt.addText(name, bold=True, italic=True, underline="thick", color="#FF0000")
    rt.addText("\n")
    rt.addText("Group ", color="#32a856", bold=True)
    rt.addText(group, color="#32a856", bold=True)

    return rt

df = pd.DataFrame(columns=["id", "group", "name"])
df.loc[0] = ["123", "A", "Bob"]
df["text"] = df.apply(createSampleRT, axis=1).astype(str)  # type: ignore

df.to_parquet("../tests/richtext/dat.parquet")

FormatOptions (_format:bool=True, prefix:str='', suffix:str='',
                comma_str:str=',', decimal_str:str='.',
                pad_zeroes_at_end:bool=True,
                return_int_if_possible:bool=False,
                accounting_notation:bool=False, ignore_na:bool=True)

Dataclass storing options/config for numerical formatting. Supports most locale conventions / currency formatting:
    _format: bool = True  # True returns str, False returns float
    prefix: str = ""
    suffix: str = ""
    comma_str: str = ","
    decimal_str: str = "."
    pad_zeroes_at_end: bool = True
    return_int_if_possible: bool = False
    accounting_notation: bool = False  # negative numbers in parentheses
    ignore_na: bool = True  # if input is null, return null

en_currency_opt = FormatOptions(prefix="$")
fr_currency_opt = FormatOptions(suffix=" $", decimal_str=",", comma_str=" ")






 fix_round (num:float|int|None, position:int=0)

Python’s built-in round function can return unexpected results. See https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#round. This function returns the same result as the Excel ROUND function.

testFixRound
with pytest.raises(Exception, match="invalid input"):
    fix_round("test", 123)  # type: ignore

assert round(23.335, 2) == 23.34
assert round(23.345, 2) == 23.34
assert fix_round(23.345, 2) == 23.35

assert round(-23.345, 2) == -23.34
assert fix_round(-23.345, 2) == -23.35

assert fix_round(1, 2) == 1
assert isinstance((fix_round(1, 2)), float)

assert fix_round(1.0, 2) == 1
assert isinstance((fix_round(1.0, 2)), float)

assert round(6789.2342335, 6) == 6789.234234
assert round(6789.2342345, 6) == 6789.234234
assert fix_round(6789.2342345, 6) == 6789.234235

assert round(-6789.2342345, 6) == -6789.234234
assert fix_round(-6789.2342345, 6) == -6789.234235

assert fix_round(0.0, 2) == 0.0
assert fix_round(-0.0, 2) == 0.0

# null input
assert fix_round(None, 5) == None  # type: ignore # noqa
assert fix_round(np.nan, 5) == None  # type: ignore # noqa
assert fix_round(pd.NaT, 5) == None  # type: ignore # noqa
assert fix_round(pd.NA, 5) == None  # type: ignore # noqa

testRoundAndFormat
assert round_and_format(123.445, 2, FormatOptions()) == "123.45"
assert round_and_format(9123.445, 2, FormatOptions()) == "9,123.45"
assert round_and_format(2123.445, 2, FormatOptions(comma_str="")) == "2123.45"
assert (
    round_and_format(123.445, 4, FormatOptions(comma_str="", pad_zeroes_at_end=True))
    == "123.4450"
)
assert round_and_format(-2342.475, 2, FormatOptions()) == "-2,342.48"

assert (
    round_and_format(2342.999, 0, FormatOptions(return_int_if_possible=True)) == "2,343"
)
assert (
    round_and_format(2342.999, 0, FormatOptions(return_int_if_possible=False))
    == "2,343.0"
)
assert (
    round_and_format(
        2342.999, 0, FormatOptions(return_int_if_possible=False, comma_str="")
    )
    == "2343.0"
)
assert round_and_format(2342.999, 0, FormatOptions(comma_str="")) == "2343.0"

assert (
    round_and_format(2342.999, 1, FormatOptions(return_int_if_possible=True)) == "2,343"
)
assert (
    round_and_format(
        2342.999, 1, FormatOptions(return_int_if_possible=True, comma_str="")
    )
    == "2343"
)
assert (
    round_and_format(2342.999, 1, FormatOptions(return_int_if_possible=False))
    == "2,343.0"
)

assert round_and_format(0.0, 0, FormatOptions()) == "0.0"

x = round_and_format(9123.445, 2, FormatOptions(_format=False))
assert isinstance(x, float)




testInvalidInputs
default_opts = FormatOptions()
with pytest.raises(Exception, match="Invalid input"):
    round_and_format("0", 0, default_opts)  # type: ignore
with pytest.raises(Exception, match="Invalid input"):
    round_and_format("abc", 0, default_opts)  # type: ignore

assert round_and_format("abc", 0, default_opts, "coerce") == None  # type: ignore # noqa
assert round_and_format("abc", 0, default_opts, "ignore") == "abc"  # type: ignore




testNullInput
x = round_and_format(None, 0, default_opts)  # type: ignore
assert x is None

x = round_and_format(np.nan, 0, default_opts)  # type: ignore
assert x is None

x = round_and_format(pd.NaT, 0, default_opts)  # type: ignore
assert x is None

x = round_and_format(pd.NA, 0, default_opts)  # type: ignore
assert x is None




testAccountingNotation
assert (
    round_and_format(
        -9123.56345, 2, FormatOptions(prefix="$", accounting_notation=True)
    )
    == "$(9,123.56)"
)
assert (
    round_and_format(9123.56345, 2, FormatOptions(prefix="$", accounting_notation=True))
    == "$9,123.56"
)
assert (
    round_and_format(
        -5.56123345,
        2,
        FormatOptions(comma_str="", suffix="%", accounting_notation=True),
    )
    == "(5.56)%"
)
assert (
    round_and_format(
        5.56123345,
        2,
        FormatOptions(comma_str=" ", suffix="%", accounting_notation=True),
    )
    == "5.56%"
)




testIgnoreNa
x = round_and_format(None, 2, FormatOptions(ignore_na=True))  # type: ignore
assert x is None

with pytest.raises(Exception, match="Invalid input"):
    x = round_and_format(None, 2, FormatOptions(ignore_na=False))  # type: ignore

assert (
    round_and_format(None, 2, FormatOptions(ignore_na=False), errors="coerce") == None  # type: ignore # noqa

assert round_and_format(123.445, 2, FormatOptions()) == "123.45"
assert round_and_format(9123.445, 2, FormatOptions()) == "9,123.45"
assert round_and_format(2123.445, 2, FormatOptions(comma_str="")) == "2123.45"

    round_and_format(123.445, 4, FormatOptions(comma_str="", pad_zeroes_at_end=True))
    == "123.4450"
)
assert round_and_format(-2342.475, 2, FormatOptions()) == "-2,342.48"

assert (
    round_and_format(2342.999, 0, FormatOptions(return_int_if_possible=True)) == "2,343"
)
assert (
    round_and_format(2342.999, 0, FormatOptions(return_int_if_possible=False))
    == "2,343.0"
)
assert (
    round_and_format(
        2342.999, 0, FormatOptions(return_int_if_possible=False, comma_str="")
    )
    == "2343.0"
)
assert round_and_format(2342.999, 0, FormatOptions(comma_str="")) == "2343.0"

assert (
    round_and_format(2342.999, 1, FormatOptions(return_int_if_possible=True)) == "2,343"
)

    round_and_format(
        2342.999, 1, FormatOptions(return_int_if_possible=True, comma_str="")
    )
    == "2343"
)
assert (
    round_and_format(2342.999, 1, FormatOptions(return_int_if_possible=False))
    == "2,343.0"
)

assert round_and_format(0.0, 0, FormatOptions()) == "0.0"

assert isinstance(x, float)

    round_and_format("0", 0, default_opts)  # type: ignore

    round_and_format("abc", 0, default_opts)  # type: ignore

assert round_and_format("abc", 0, default_opts, "coerce") == None  # type: ignore # noqa
assert round_and_format("abc", 0, default_opts, "ignore") == "abc"  # type: ignore

x = round_and_format(None, 0, default_opts)  # type: ignore
assert x is None

assert x is None

x = round_and_format(pd.NA, 0, default_opts)  # type: ignore
assert x is None




testAccountingNotation

    round_and_format(
        -9123.56345, 2, FormatOptions(prefix="$", accounting_notation=True)
    )
    == "$(9,123.56)"
)
assert (
    round_and_format(9123.56345, 2, FormatOptions(prefix="$", accounting_notation=True))
    == "$9,123.56"
)
assert (
    round_and_format(
        -5.56123345,
        2,
        FormatOptions(comma_str="", suffix="%", accounting_notation=True),
    )
    == "(5.56)%"
)
assert (
    round_and_format(
        5.56123345,
        2,
        FormatOptions(comma_str=" ", suffix="%", accounting_notation=True),
    )
    == "5.56%"
)




testIgnoreNa
x = round_and_format(None, 2, FormatOptions(ignore_na=True))  # type: ignore
assert x is None

with pytest.raises(Exception, match="Invalid input"):
    x = round_and_format(None, 2, FormatOptions(ignore_na=False))  # type: ignore

assert (
    round_and_format(None, 2, FormatOptions(ignore_na=False), errors="coerce") == None  # type: ignore # noqa
)
assert (
    round_and_format(None, 2, FormatOptions(ignore_na=False), errors="ignore") == None  # type: ignore # noqa
)

title: Images
text:
Example usage

def addDynamicLogoColumn(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """-> pd.DataFrame

    Parameters
    ----------
    df : pd.DataFrame
        pd.DataFrame

    Returns
    -------
    pd.DataFrame
        pd.DataFrame
    """
    logo1 = Image("../tests/images/logo1.png", width_mm=40)
    logo2 = Image("../tests/images/logo2.png", width_mm=40)

    df["img_logo"] = logo1  # will need to specify this is an image col in cfg file
    m = df["group"] == "2"  # type: ignore # noqa
    df.loc[m, "img_logo"] = logo2  # type: ignore # noqa

    df["img_logo"] = df["img_logo"].apply(lambda x: asdict(x))

    return df


df = pd.DataFrame(columns=["id", "group"])
df.loc[0] = ["1", "1"]
df.loc[1] = ["2", "2"]

df = df.pipe(addDynamicLogoColumn).copy()
df.to_parquet("../tests/images/dat.parquet")

df["img_logo"] = df["img_logo"].apply(lambda x: hidePaths(x))
